properties.name: ROOT CAUSE: a release tag cannot publish the site, because the github-pages environment admits main alone (v0.84.0's tag run refused)
properties.source: GitHub Actions: pages run 38555276998 attempt 1, check run 115823407360 (its annotations); the github-pages environment read through the REST API
properties.statement:
ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured 2026-10-14 on GitHub): the first release after #741 could not republish reflow2's site from its tag. #741 (58ec32bac) added `tags: ["v*"]` to .github/workflows/pages.yml so that each release tag would republish the site and the home page's counts (tools/site_counts.py) would take in the release just cut. The repository's `github-pages` environment admits deployments from `main` alone: one custom policy, main, type branch. Anthony keeps that on purpose.

1 OBSERVED: pages run 38555276998, attempt 1, on tag v0.84.0 (job 115823407360, 11:17:03 to 11:17:05Z). GitHub's own annotations, level failure: "Tag "v0.84.0" is not allowed to deploy to github-pages due to environment protection rules." and "The deployment was rejected or didn't satisfy other protection rules." Expected: the site republished with v0.84.0 counted.
NOT AFFECTED: main's pages run 38555256320 at the same commit (e62dfd291), created 11:15:10Z, deployed, and its counts.json already ended at v0.84.0. That was luck of order: it started before the tag was pushed. A cut's merge always comes before its tag, so main's run can miss the new release.

2 PRECEDENT: search_design on the raw annotation, in reflow2 and in flo2: nothing.

3 CANDIDATES: (a) the tag trigger meets the main-only environment; (b) Pages itself is misconfigured; (c) another protection rule (reviewers, a wait timer) rejected it; (d) the observation is wrong.

4-5 MEASURED: (b) refuted, since main's run at the same commit deployed ten seconds earlier. (c) refuted, since the environment's protection_rules hold branch_policy alone. (d) refuted, since the annotation names the tag and the environment, and attempt 2 of the same run (12:13Z), re-run while a temporary v* tag policy was in place, deployed. That policy was then removed. (a) stands, and the evidence is GitHub's own annotation.

6 CLASS: the trigger lives in the repository, and the environment that decides whether it may deploy lives in repository settings. Nothing checked one against the other.

7 PINNED: tools/test_release_workflow.py, test_the_site_is_published_from_main_and_never_from_a_tag and test_the_release_dispatches_the_site_on_main_after_publishing. Both seen failing on origin/main fb996824b (11/13 passed).
